land.text: Duklja as a Byzantine province: toparchy 'of the Dalmatian kastra of Zeta and Ston' held by Vojislav, who revolted c. 1034

predecessors.note: Vojislav page: 'Before his revolt, Duklja was under Byzantine control'; the Duklja page: 'After the Byzantines defeated the Bulgarians in 1018, Duklja fell back under Byzantine rule'. An earlier Doclean polity existed from the late 10th century (Samuel invaded it in 997 and made Vladimir a vassal).

land.text: Duklja's territory annexed by Stefan Nemanja in 1186

successors.note: The Duklja page: 'Conquered by the Grand Principality of Serbia, 1186/9'; Nemanja's state is carried in Cliopatria by the Kingdom of Serbia row from 1188 (grand-principality-of-serbia ends in this project's dossiers at 1168, when Cliopatria's Grand Principality row ends).

capitals.name: Skadar (Shkodër), with Bar
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Bar (Shkodër)'; the Vojislav page names Skadar as the capital with courts at Trebinje, Kotor and Bar. The pages date no move between the two.

rulers.name: Stefan Vojislav
rulers.title: knez
rulers.note: Seized Duklja c. 1034, captured 1035/1036, escaped late 1037/early 1038, died 1043.

rulers.name: Mihailo Vojislavljevic
rulers.title: knez, king from 1077
rulers.note: Succeeded as knez in 1046; 'In 1077, he received a crown from Pope Gregory VII'; the 1043-1046 interval is not covered.

rulers.name: Constantine Bodin
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: 'On Constantine Bodin's death in 1101 or possibly 1108'; civil war followed.

rulers.name: Radoslav
rulers.title: knez
rulers.note: 'Radoslav (1146-1149) bore only the title of knez'; Gradinja was the last to hold the title of king.

correction.text: Vojislav's state: the coast from Ston to Skadar and its hinterland, 1034-1055

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Duklja shape begins in 1056, but Vojislav revolted from Byzantium c. 1034 ('about this time'), was imprisoned 1035/1036, escaped late 1037/early 1038, and 'by 1040 his state stretched in the coastal region from Ston in the north' to Skadar, with courts at Trebinje, Kotor and Bar; Travunia and Zahumlje were under partial control. The 1056 shape is carried back; Mihailo's 1046 succession changes nothing territorial. The infobox gives no area.

8.6 thousand km2 under Mihailo (knez from 1046, protospatharios 1050). The Mihailo page gives no borders; the Vojislav page describes the coast from Ston to Skadar, which matches the bbox (17.51-19.72E, 41.85-43.15N). The Duklja page's infobox has no area.

28.3 thousand km2, +20 thousand: Raska. The Duklja page has Mihailo 'conquered Raska from the Byzantines in the 1060s'; the Mihailo page does not mention Raska. The year 1066 is Cliopatria's; the page gives only the decade. Kept.

28.3 thousand km2, the same outline. Cliopatria changes the name in 1072 but the royal crown came in 1077: 'In 1077, he received a crown from Pope Gregory VII' (a letter of 9 January 1078 calls him 'king of the Slavs'). The shape is not affected; the ledger's rename is 1077.

50.0 thousand km2, +22 thousand, with the bbox reaching 44.97N and 17.34E: Bosnia. The Bodin page cites the Chronicle of Dioclea for Bodin's conquest of Rascia 'in this decade' (the 1080s) and for campaigns in Bosnia and Serbia where he installed relatives (no year); the Duklja page says Bodin 'also took Bosnia'. The year 1085 is Cliopatria's; the Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja is a disputed source. Holds 1085-1090.

correction.text: Duklja's core after Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia broke away: the 1094 shape held from 1091

keyframe_review.note: 9.0 thousand km2: the core only. The Duklja page has Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia 'probably broke away after 1090' and the Grand Principality page has Vukan independent 'in 1091 or 1092, taking the title of Grand Prince'; Cliopatria shows the loss in 1094. Corrected: the same outline from 1091 (1091-1125).
9.0 thousand km2, the same outline, for 1126-1138: Grubesa ruled 1118-1125, Gradinja was the last king. Kept.

New keyframe for 1139-1185: Cliopatria drops Duklja after 1138, but the Duklja page has it continuing: Radoslav (1146-1149) as knez, 'In 1150, Desa was mentioned in a charter as dux of Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje' (Grand Principality page), 'By 1166 much of Duklja was under Raska', annexed by Nemanja in 1186. The 1126 outline is extended; the page names no land lost by 1166. Contested with Raska by the ledger from 1150.

region.text: the core around Skadar (Zeta), Vojislav's toparchy of Zeta and Ston

ledger.note: c. 1034: Stefan Vojislav revolts and Duklja breaks from Byzantium. 'Following John Skylitzes, Duklja's break from Byzantine rule is dated to about this time'; the Duklja page has him seize Duklja in 1034; he had been Byzantine 'toparch of Zeta and Ston' since 1018.

region.text: Duklja, fought over by Vojislav and Byzantium 1034-1042

ledger.note: c. 1034: the Byzantine war for Duklja begins. Vojislav is 'defeated and imprisoned in Constantinople in 1035/1036', escapes 'in late 1037 or early 1038' and 'liberated most of Duklja' (Duklja page).

region.text: the coast from Ston to Skadar and its hinterland

ledger.note: By 1040: Vojislav holds the coast from Ston to Skadar. 'By 1040 his state stretched in the coastal region from Ston in the north', with courts at Trebinje, Kotor and Bar; he asserted 'partial control' over Travunia and Zahumlje.

region.text: Duklja, fought over by Vojislav and Byzantium 1034-1042

ledger.note: 1042: Vojislav defeats Constantine IX's coalition. 'The battle took place in the mountainous area between Bar and Crmnica after midnight in 1042'; he 'spent the rest of his rule in peace and died in 1043'.

region.text: Raska, conquered from the Byzantines in the 1060s

ledger.note: 1060s: Mihailo conquers Raska from the Byzantines. 'Mihailo secured rule by 1046 and conquered Raska from the Byzantines in the 1060s'; the year 1066 is Cliopatria's shape change, the page gives the decade.

1077: Mihailo receives a crown from Pope Gregory VII and Duklja becomes a kingdom. 'In 1077, he received a crown from Pope Gregory VII'; a letter of 9 January 1078 addresses him as 'Michael, king of the Slavs'.

minus.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Duklja shape of 1085
Cliopatria's Kingdom of Duklja shape of 1084

region.text: the lands added to the 1084 shape in 1085: Bosnia and its marches

ledger.note: 1080s: Bodin extends Duklja into Bosnia. The Duklja page: 'Bodin also took Bosnia'; the Bodin page cites the Chronicle of Dioclea for his conquest of Rascia in the 1080s and campaigns in Bosnia where he installed relatives (no year). 1085 is Cliopatria's shape change; the source is disputed.

region.text: Raska, with Vukan as Grand Prince

ledger.note: 1091: Vukan makes Raska independent. 'In 1091 or 1092, Vukan became independent, taking the title of Grand Prince'; Bodin had installed Vukan and Marko as zupans there (Bodin page).

After 1090: Zahumlje and Bosnia break away. 'Raska, Zahumlje, and Bosnia probably broke away after 1090' (the Byzantines punished Bodin in 1090 and imprisoned him again). The year is the page's lower bound.

1150: Raska's Desa appears as ruler of Duklja. 'In 1150, Desa was mentioned in a charter as dux of Duklja, Travunija and Zahumlje' (Grand Principality page); 'By 1166 much of Duklja was under Raska' (Duklja page). Which lands is not stated.
1186: Stefan Nemanja annexes Duklja. 'Stefan Nemanja annexed Duklja after defeating the last Doclean prince, Mihailo, in 1186.' (Princess Desislava is listed as ruler 1186-1189, disputed.)
1186: the last Doclean land passes to Nemanja's Serbia. Infobox: 'Conquered by the Grand Principality of Serbia, 1186/9'.
1186: Duklja ends. Annexed by Stefan Nemanja; the Duklja page's infobox gives the end as 1186/9.

wars.name: Revolt of Stefan Vojislav against Byzantium
wars.outcome: Vojislav is defeated and imprisoned in 1035/1036, escapes in 1037/1038, liberates most of Duklja and defeats the Byzantine coalition between Bar and Crmnica in 1042.
wars.note: The Duklja page dates the seizure to 1034, not 1035.

wars.name: Uprising of Georgi Voiteh (Bodin's expedition)
wars.outcome: Mihailo sends Bodin with 300 troops; Bodin is crowned emperor of the Bulgarians as Petar, takes part in the revolt in Pomoravlje and Povardarje, is captured and freed in 1078; no border change.
wars.note: The Mihailo page puts the sending in the fall of 1072.

wars.name: Byzantine punishment of Bodin

zones.text: Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia, which broke away

wars.outcome: The Byzantines, after dealing with the Normans, defeat Bodin and imprison him again; Raska, Zahumlje and Bosnia probably break away after 1090.
wars.note: The Bodin page gives no year for the attack; the Duklja page has 'In 1090 the Byzantines punished him'.

wars.name: Succession wars after Bodin and Raska's intervention
wars.outcome: Dobroslav II, Kocopar, Vladimir and Djuradj contend; Vukan of Raska helps Kocopar defeat Dobroslav then drives Kocopar out; the Byzantines install Grubesa in 1118 (to 1125); Uros of Raska restores Djuradj.
wars.note: The page gives no years for the Raskan interventions beyond 1118-1125 for Grubesa.

certainty.note: The Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja is a disputed source for the extent under Mihailo and Bodin; no treaty lines are on the pages opened, so the Bosnian and Rascian marches are approximate throughout.

notes: Page budget (5) spent on Duklja, Constantine Bodin, Stefan Vojislav, Mihailo I of Duklja and the Grand Principality of Serbia article (shared with that dossier). One state: Wikidata Q1252942 is shared by the two Cliopatria rows 'Great Principality of Duklja' (1056-1071) and 'Kingdom of Duklja' (1072-1138); the Duklja page calls the polity one continuous Doclean state (knez, then king from 1077) and the phrase 'Great Principality of Duklja' does not appear on it, so there is one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names. Cliopatria ends Duklja in 1138 but the page keeps it to 1186; the 1139-1185 keyframe extends the 1126 shape and is the most doubtful stretch. The state starts here in 1034 (Vojislav's revolt), not in the late 10th century (Jovan Vladimir, Samuel's 997 invasion; Byzantine again after 1018), which the pages date only vaguely and Cliopatria does not draw. The Byzantine overlordship over Mihailo (protospatharios 1050; 'ally and friend of the Byzantines'; Byzantine nominee Grubesa 1118-1125) and Duklja's suzerainty over Raska/Bosnia/Zahumlje are not written as vassal events; they belong to the byzantine-empire and Raska dossiers. Counterpart grand-principality-of-serbia is the page's name for Nemanja's annexing state, which this project's dossier of that slug ends in 1168 (Cliopatria's row), so the 1150-1186 contest has no mirror there: the kingdom-of-serbia dossier (eu-18) should mirror it. Gazetteer names needed: Duklja (Zeta), Travunia, Zahumlje (alias of Herzegovina exists), Crmnica, Bar.
